ledger.note: 1568: Hadiwijaya (Jaka Tingkir) founds the Kingdom of Pajang. 'In 1568, after Penangsang was killed, Hadiwijaya assumed the role of sovereign'; 'he moved all of Demak's regalia, heirlooms, and sacred artifacts to Pajang'; 'Thus the Demak Sultanate ended with the foundation of the short-lived Kingdom of Pajang'. The infobox of the Pajang page shows 1568. The land is the Pajang page's list of places, not a boundary.

region.text: Demak, the former capital on the north coast, now under Sunan Pangiri as adipati

ledger.note: 1568: Demak becomes a vassal of Pajang. 'Pajang became the suzerain kingdom, while Demak became its vassal'; Hadiwijaya 'appointed Prawata's son Sunan Pangiri as adipati of Demak'. A 30 km circle round the town of Demak (a gazetteer place).
1586: Demak's vassalage ends with Pajang's. Page silent on Demak after 1568: the date is the end of Pajang.

region.text: Central Java: Pengging (Boyolali and Klaten), Tingkir (Salatiga), Butuh (Purworejo) and surrounding areas; the palace at Pajang near Kartasura

ledger.note: 1586: Banawa submits Pajang's crown to Sutawijaya. Ario Pangiri's rebellion forced Banawa to seek help from Sutawijaya, who defeated Ario Pangiri and seized the Pajang palace, and Banawa 'submitted his crown to Sutawijaya', ending Pajang in 1586; Sutawijaya founded Mataram in 1586. The infobox's '1586-1587' entry and Cliopatria's 1587 conflict.

wars.name: Demak succession war
wars.outcome: Trenggana died in 1546; Arya Penangsang of Jipang killed Sunan Prawata and took the Demak throne in 1549 (Demak page); he was killed with Sutawijaya's and Ki Ageng Pamanahan's help, and Hadiwijaya took the sovereignty in 1568.
wars.note: Penangsang's reign is 1549-1568 in the text and 1547-1554 in the family tree; the Pajang page has him killed by Sutawijaya and Ki Ageng Pamanahan, undated.

wars.name: Pangiri's rebellion and the fall of Pajang
wars.outcome: Sutawijaya defeated Ario Pangiri, seized the palace and received Banawa's crown: Pajang ends and Mataram begins (1586).
wars.note: No territorial detail on the page.

certainty.note: A Central Java court with undefined tributary Java around it; no boundary on any page.

notes:
Two pages opened (budget 1-2). 'Kingdom of Pajana' is the Pajang kingdom of Central Java; Cliopatria's Wikipedia title 'Lontara script' (the Bugis-Makassar script) and Wikidata Q1074947 look like a mismatch (wikidata is unreachable): the colour/state-page agents should use 'Pajang Sultanate'.
CLIOPATRIA: the 1572-1587 shapes are the same 175-cell polygon as Demak 1551 and Mataram 1588; I cut the 59 East Java cells because neither page places a Pajang holding there, and added 1568-1571 because the Demak page puts the foundation in 1568 (Cliopatria's Demak ends 1551, leaving 1552-1571 empty). The Demak dossier should settle whether Demak ends 1551 (Cliopatria) or 1568 (page), and the Mataram dossier whether Mataram starts 1586 (Pajang page) or 1588 (Cliopatria): 1587 is a one-year gap or overlap.
PAGE SILENT: capital, area, reign years (the infobox shows 1568-1583, 1583-1586, 1586-1587, unattached to rulers; no rulers list is written), the date of Sutawijaya's fief at Alas Mentaok, East Java and Madura relations, the 1581 recognition, the 1582 and 1587 events, Banten and Cirebon relations. Jipang (Arya Penangsang's vassal state) has no dossier.
Gazetteer: Pengging, Tingkir (Salatiga is a place), Butuh, Alas Mentaok and Pajang are not in the gazetteer; Demak is.
